You will own the complete embedded hardware and firmware stack—from schematics and high-density multilayer layouts to the real-time C/C++ firmware running directly on the metal.

Fitting multiple drives, high-density tactile arrays, and power electronics into a hand-sized volume means every decision is a tight balance of space, thermals, signal integrity, and manufacturability. You will work closely with the CTO and cross-functional team, moving smoothly between architecture, circuit design, and the lab to solve complex problems where physics meets code.

What you will do:

  • Own the hardware architecture. Design schematics and high-density, multilayer PCB layouts (mixed-signal, tight thermal/EMC constraints) built for modularity across product variants—not a one-off prototype.

  • Build control hardware and firmware that can't miss a beat. Search, evaluate, test, and integrate actuator hardware alongside motor drivers for compact servo drives; write deterministic real-time firmware (C/C++) for control loops, timing-critical execution, limit monitoring, and fault handling.

  • Choose the right sensor and make the data mean something. Search, evaluate, test, and integrate sensor hardware for tactile sensing and proprioception (position and force); design low-noise readout electronics, signal conditioning, filtering, and calibration pipelines to deliver clean, low-latency telemetry to the software stack.

  • Ship rock-solid bootloaders and drivers. Build field-updatable bootloaders, low-level drivers, and secure, fail-safe update strategies across product generations—documented and reliable, not tribal knowledge.

  • Build interfaces customers actually want to integrate. Implement and maintain fieldbus and hardware communication layers (EtherCAT, CANopen, Ethernet) aligned cleanly with higher-level software and robot controllers.

  • Debug on real hardware. Own the lab bring-up process from first power-on to full validation. Trace issues across the hardware, firmware, and mechanical boundaries with scopes, logic analyzers, and thermal imaging.

  • Build security into the product from day one. Support Cyber Resilience Act compliance by integrating secure boot, signed firmware updates, and hardware-level trust mechanisms early in the design cycle.

  • Build for series production, not just the lab. Design for manufacturing and test (DFM/DFT), select resilient supply-chain components with second sources, run EMC pre-compliance, and drive hardware through production ramp-up.

  • Work across the whole team. Tight loop with Mechanics, Software, and System Applications—translating mechanical and control requirements into robust, deployable electronics.

  • A degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, Robotics, or a related field.

  • Proven expertise in schematic capture and multilayer PCB layout (Altium, KiCad, or similar), specifically for space-constrained, mixed-signal designs.

  • Strong C/C++ skills on bare-metal or RTOS (ARM Cortex-M or similar) with a deep understanding of timing, concurrency, memory, and register-level hardware control.

  • A strong hardware mindset: you enjoy lab bring-up, signal-integrity debugging, and getting to the bottom of transient issues with a scope or logic analyzer.

  • Fluent English; German is a plus, not a requirement.

Bonus:

  • Miniature electronics, high-density PCB packaging, or tight thermal constraints

  • Tactile, force/torque, or contact-rich sensor arrays

  • Real-time fieldbuses (EtherCAT, CANopen)

  • Product security: secure boot, signed firmware, CRA, IEC 62443

  • Functional safety standards (Machinery Regulation, ISO/TS 15066)

The next chapter of robotics won't be built in a lab. It will be built by people who care about what happens when technology meets the real world.

That means your decisions will have a lasting impact — not just on a product, but on what comes next for Physical AI.

Build the hand. Define the standard. Shape what comes next.

If you're excited by the challenge of building robotic hands that work reliably in the real world, we'd love to hear from you.

description:

Modern conflict runs on the electromagnetic spectrum, and the systems that listen to it have to survive the real world. Datacept builds cognitive electronic warfare systems: passive wideband sensing, AI-driven signal analysis, deployed at ports, stadiums, critical infrastructure, and military sites.

Our systems are already in use with customers. Now the hardware has to scale: produced repeatedly, refined, and trusted in the field.

We are looking for a working student who can take it there: someone who designs the part in CAD and then makes it on the machine.

Your role

You are the hands of our hardware team. You take our existing hardware and develop it into the next generation: robust, manufacturable, well-designed. You work directly with the founders and the engineers, you make design decisions, and you build your own parts in our workshop instead of waiting for someone else to.

What you will do

  • Develop our current hardware into a series-ready next generation: construction, assemblies, tolerances, materials

  • Product design: enclosures, ergonomics, surfaces, mounting, and ease of assembly in the field

  • Create CAD models, technical drawings, and bills of materials

  • Build prototypes and samples yourself on our in-house CNC mill and 3D printers, plus assembly and functional tests

  • Test hardware under real conditions, learn from failures, and iterate quickly

  • Coordinate with suppliers and manufacturing partners on what works in series production

How we work

  • Build, don't just draw. An idea becomes a part in your hand before it becomes a document.

  • Fast learners over specific backgrounds. We care more about how quickly you pick up new skills than where you have worked before.

  • Intellectual honesty. The right answer matters more than being right. If the test shows the design fails, we change the design.

  • Ownership of outcomes. You organise your own time, focus on what matters, and cut out inefficiencies. Nobody manages your calendar for you.

  • Not building in a vacuum. You stay connected to the founders, the software and RF team, and the sites where our systems run, so that all the pieces fit together in the field.

Requirements

  • You study mechanical engineering, product design, mechatronics, or a similar field

  • You have strong CAD skills (e.g. SolidWorks, Fusion 360, Inventor)

  • You have built real hardware, not only modelled it

  • You have operated a CNC mill, or you are ready to learn it on ours

  • You understand design for manufacturing

  • You go from idea to prototype on your own, and you ask for help when it speeds things up rather than when you are stuck

  • You are available up to 20 hours per week during the semester, more during semester breaks if you want

Helpful, not required

  • Basic CAM knowledge (e.g. Fusion 360 CAM)

  • Experience with FDM or resin 3D printing, turning, sheet metal, or composites

  • Electronics basics: wiring, sensors, integrating PCBs and antennas into enclosures

  • Projects you built yourself: maker work, Formula Student, university teams, a portfolio

  • Rendering and visual design

  • Experience with rugged or outdoor hardware

  • You want to contribute to Europe's technological sovereignty in a domain where it is currently lacking

Benefits

  • Work on a real product that ends up in real deployments

  • Your own workshop with a CNC mill and 3D printers: design a part in the morning, hold it in your hand by the afternoon

  • Flexible hours around lectures and exams

  • Compensation: €16–20 per hour

  • 6-month contract with the option to extend

  • Perspective for a thesis or a long-term role as we grow

  • Insight into real RF hardware and field deployments

  • Workshop and main workplace in Horneburg (R&D). Days without hands-on work can be done from our Hamburg HafenCity HQ

Hiring process

  1. Intro call (15 min, remote): who you are, why Datacept

  2. Project conversation (45 min): bring what you built (CAD, photos, parts), and we start with a small design challenge right away

  3. Final meeting in person at our workshop in Horneburg with the founders

  4. Reference check and offer within 48 hours

About Datacept

Datacept GmbH, founded in Hamburg in 2025, builds cognitive electronic warfare systems for spectrum awareness, counter-drone defence, and the protection of critical infrastructure. Our platform unifies passive wideband sensing, AI-driven signal analysis, and the RF data infrastructure that ties them together.

We have raised pre-seed capital and are backed by German federal funding. We work with critical infrastructure operators, defence agencies, and NATO partners to give Europe the intelligence we need in the electromagnetic spectrum.

PERGOLUX designs and sells premium, Scandinavian-inspired outdoor living products, from aluminium pergolas to awnings and garden furniture, directly to consumers. We are a company that has grown consistently across Europe and beyond, with around 300 employees, 9-figure revenue and operations across eight markets.

What You'll Do

- Analyse the full funnel (lead, contact, qualification, draft order, order) by market, tier, channel and rep, mine call, chat and CRM activity for conversion patterns, and run a monthly insight cycle of three to five prioritised findings, each with an owner, an action and a measured result.

- Own the global capacity model for Tier 1, Tier 2, showroom and Customer Service fallback coverage, run the monthly refresh and seasonal peak plan, and flag hiring, reallocation or BPO volume changes early while tracking planned versus actual coverage with Sales Leads and Finance.

- Run the monthly and quarterly bonus calculations for Sales Leads, Tier 2 reps and the Tier 1 partner payout, test and model each scheme before changes go live, and automate the calculation and reporting so payouts need checks rather than manual builds.

- Own revenue per worked hour as the core productivity KPI, from definition and baseline to targets and monthly reporting by market and tier, and lead initiatives that move its drivers of productive time, conversion and order value.

- Orchestrate sales activity through task queues, lead prioritisation, follow-up cadences and reactivation, map and automate our sales processes in HubSpot (with Aircall, Shopify and messaging integrations), and run AI pilots across the funnel with clear success metrics and a running business case per use case.

What You'll Bring

- Proven experience in sales operations, revenue operations or GTM engineering, turning sales, call and order data into decisions and measurable KPI movement.

- Strong analytical skills across the full funnel, with the ability to write clear requirements for a data team and validate what they ship.

- Hands-on experience building HubSpot workflows and integrations with tools such as Aircall, Shopify and messaging platforms, within agreed data governance.

- A builder-operator mindset: you design capacity models, incentive schemes and process automation, then operate and iterate on them rather than only reporting.

- Practical experience deploying AI use cases across a sales funnel (speed-to-lead, qualification, summaries, next-best-action, follow-up drafting) is a strong plus.

💼 Compensation — Attractive, competitive salary · Company pension plan · Capped overtime, fully paid, with no endless unpaid crunch · 20% commission on base salary plus a maximum 30% additional bonus for exceeding targets

🚀 Growth and Career Development — You will take real ownership from the start with direct impact on key revenue outcomes, work alongside an international, collaborative team across Europe, and have a fast-track path to grow into senior leadership as PERGOLUX scales.

⏰ Time Off and Flexibility — Up to 30 vacation days, starting at 27 · One week per year remote workation in the EU/UK

🌟 Benefits and Lifestyle

- Regular team events (summer party, Christmas party, after-work gatherings) and retreats

- Modern setup and laptops (Apple or Windows)

- Employee discounts on PERGOLUX products

- Jobrad / Bike leasing program, promoting sustainable and healthy commuting

📍 Office Location – Schlesische Str. 27 C, Building C, 6th floor, 10997 Berlin

How to Apply

If you want to own how our sales engine plans, automates and scales, we would like to hear from you. Apply through our [Career Page](https://pergolux.careers/) or connect with us on [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/pergolux/posts/?feedView=all).
